content.comment_body: I'm rewriting a program with internal marker coils and inputs, but I can't figure out how these were originally added to the ladder logic. The program doesn't seem to be written in function block diagram—how can I recreate this?

Hello, This is a drawback of working in ladder logic compared to function block diagram. Internal markers (flags) are used to complete one relay coil line and then use the result as a normally closed contact on another line. These flags operate internally. In function block diagram, direct graphical connections eliminate the need for such markers. To use internal markers in ladder logic, add a coil and then select 'IM' from the dropdown or type it at the top of the list. There are no restrictions on the number of internal markers, but you need to keep track of which numbers you are using. In my opinion, programming with function block diagram is much simpler than with ladder logic. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience uncertainty about handling internal marker coils and inputs when converting programs between ladder logic and function block diagram formats in [company_name]'s automation software. Specifically, the challenge is in understanding how internal markers are managed in ladder logic versus the more intuitive graphical connections available in function block diagrams, which impacts usability for those switching between these methods.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want straightforward, user-friendly ways to replicate internal markers in ladder logic, with tools that make finding and reusing internal markers easier, and generally smoother transitions between different program representation formats.
